title: A Riviera Week from a Monaco Base

bestPeriod.note: Avoid the last week of May entirely; the Grand Prix closes half the streets and triples every room rate.

summary: Monaco is 2 km² and takes a day and a half. Base there and let the Ventimiglia-Cannes railway deliver a different Riviera town every morning.
hook: Monaco is two square kilometres. You can walk it end to end in forty-five minutes, and after two days you will have seen it properly. The reason to stay is the railway: a two-track line hugging the coast from Ventimiglia to Cannes, with Monaco-Monte-Carlo in the middle, putting six other towns within half an hour.

snapshot.Country: Monaco (with days in France and Italy)
snapshot.Best Period: April to June, September and October
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 55-70 km on foot, steep and stepped; roughly 6 hours on TER trains
snapshot.Getting There: Nice airport, then tram T2 to Nice-Ville and TER to Monaco, about 55 min total
snapshot.Who It Suits: Belle Époque and modernist architecture readers, coastal-path walkers, people who dislike hire cars

itinerary.title: Le Rocher and Fontvieille
itinerary.morning: The Rocher is the old town on its 60 m limestone headland, one walkable block: Rue Basse, Place de la Visitation, and the Cathédrale de Monaco (Charles Lenormand, 1875) with Rainier III and Grace Kelly's tombs. The guard changes on Place du Palais at 11:55 daily.
itinerary.afternoon: The Musée Océanographique, opened 1910 to Paul Delefortrie's design and run by Jacques Cousteau from 1957 to 1988, is the serious institution here: approx €21, timed slots online. Walk down through the Jardins Saint-Martin afterwards to see its sheer sea facade.
itinerary.evening: Down the ramp to Fontvieille for the Princess Grace Rose Garden and the port. Marché de la Condamine on Place d'Armes, a covered hall trading since 1880, does barbagiuan and socca at its counters until mid-afternoon, and the restaurants around it run late.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking, 200 m of climbing and public lifts · districts: Rocher, Fontvieille, Condamine · tickets approx €21.

itinerary.title: Monte-Carlo and Larvotto
itinerary.morning: The Casino de Monte-Carlo (Charles Garnier, 1878-79) opens for self-guided daytime visits from 10:00 to about 13:00, approx €18, and that is the only way to see the Salle Garnier opera house and the Salle Blanche without gambling. Bring a passport: ID is checked at the door, and 18 is the minimum age even for the tour.
itinerary.afternoon: The Jardins du Casino, the Hôtel de Paris (1864) and the Café de Paris (1868), then east to the Nouveau Musée National de Monaco's Villa Sauber on Avenue Princesse Grace, approx €6.
itinerary.evening: Larvotto beach, rebuilt in 2020, and the Japanese Garden. Dinner on the Port Hercule quays.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking · districts: Monte-Carlo, Larvotto · tickets approx €24.

itinerary.title: Nice: Vieux-Nice, Cimiez and the Promenade
itinerary.morning: TER to Nice-Ville, 22 minutes, roughly €5.20. Walk down to Cours Saleya: flower and produce market Tuesday to Sunday, about 06:00 to 13:30, antiques on Mondays. Eat socca standing up.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the free lift at the east end of Quai des États-Unis to the Colline du Château, then bus 5 to Cimiez for the Musée Matisse in its seventeenth-century villa and the Musée Marc Chagall (André Hermant, 1973), built around the Biblical Message cycle.
itinerary.evening: The Promenade des Anglais past the Hôtel Negresco (Édouard-Jean Niermans, 1913) at sunset, then the last TER back, services run until roughly 23:30.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km walking · districts: Vieux-Nice, Cimiez, Promenade · tickets approx €22 (train, Lignes d'Azur bus, two museums).

itinerary.title: Menton and Ventimiglia
itinerary.morning: TER east to Menton, 11 minutes, about €3. The old town climbs in ramps to the Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange (1675) and the cemetery terrace above. The Halles municipales on Quai de Monléon, an 1898 market building, is the food anchor: Menton lemons, tourte de blettes, pissaladière.
itinerary.afternoon: The Jardin Botanique Val Rahmeh, approx €7, or the Serre de la Madone above town. Both are the reason Menton has a microclimate reputation.
itinerary.evening: On a Friday, take the TER 12 minutes further into Italy to Ventimiglia, whose market spreads along Via Roma and the seafront until about 13:00, so go in the morning and reverse this day. Otherwise stay in Menton for an aperitif on Place aux Herbes.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walking, 120 m ascent · districts: Menton old town, Garavan; Ventimiglia · tickets approx €12.

itinerary.title: Èze, the Chemin de Nietzsche and La Turbie
itinerary.morning: TER west to Èze-sur-Mer, 9 minutes. The Chemin de Nietzsche climbs from the seafront to Èze-Village: 1.6 km, about 430 m of ascent, 60-75 minutes, rough and stepped, no water. Nietzsche said he composed part of Zarathustra on it.
itinerary.afternoon: Èze-Village at 427 m is one vertical block of lanes ending in the Jardin Exotique d'Èze, approx €8, cactus terraces over Cap Ferrat. The Fragonard perfumery below runs free factory visits.
itinerary.evening: A Zou! bus or short taxi up to La Turbie for the Trophée d'Auguste, raised in 6 BC to mark Augustus's subjugation of the Alpine tribes, then down to Monaco in about 25 minutes.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking, 520 m ascent · districts: Èze-sur-Mer, Èze-Village, La Turbie · tickets approx €14.

itinerary.title: Villefranche, Beaulieu and Cap Ferrat
itinerary.morning: TER to Villefranche-sur-Mer, 13 minutes. Jean Cocteau decorated the Chapelle Saint-Pierre on the quay in 1957; the covered thirteenth-century Rue Obscure runs under the old town; the Citadelle Saint-Elme dates from 1557.
itinerary.afternoon: One stop to Beaulieu-sur-Mer for Villa Kérylos, Emmanuel Pontremoli's 1902-08 reconstruction of a Delian Greek house, approx €13. Then bus 15 to Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild on Cap Ferrat (Aaron Messiah, 1912), approx €18: nine gardens and fountains that perform every twenty minutes. Book online in July and August.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Sentier du Littoral round Cap Ferrat toward Saint-Jean, then the train home.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km walking · districts: Villefranche old town, Beaulieu, Cap Ferrat · tickets approx €36.

itinerary.title: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin and the modernist cape
itinerary.morning: TER to Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, 6 minutes. Cap Moderne is the guided-only site holding Eileen Gray's Villa E-1027 (1929) and Le Corbusier's Cabanon (1952). Small groups, booked through the Centre des monuments nationaux, approx €18, sold out weeks ahead, book the moment your dates are fixed.
itinerary.afternoon: The Promenade Le Corbusier runs around the cape toward Monaco; then climb to Roquebrune village and its tenth-century keep, the oldest in France.
itinerary.evening: Back into Monaco to walk the Grand Prix circuit on foot: Sainte-Dévote, the hill to Casino Square, the tunnel, the harbour chicane. Forty minutes, no charge.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walking, 250 m ascent · districts: Cap Martin, Roquebrune village · tickets approx €22.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Ambassador Monaco
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes from the Condamine market and the port, five from a station exit, and far below Carré d'Or rates. The practical base: you can walk home from anywhere in the principality.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 10-12 weeks ahead; never for Grand Prix week.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Métropole Monte-Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: An 1889 building beside the Casino gardens, with a rooftop pool. Worth it only if the Belle Époque evening is the point of the trip; otherwise the money buys three days elsewhere.

accommodationStrategy.name: Beausoleil across the border
accommodationStrategy.description: Beausoleil is Monaco's uphill French twin, one street away. Rates run 40-50% lower, the public lifts drop you into Monte-Carlo in ten minutes, and you pay French rather than Monégasque restaurant prices.

logistics.emergency: 112 across all three countries. In Monaco, 17 for police and 18 for fire and ambulance. Sea rescue on VHF 16.

other.label: The railway is the trip
other.text: TER Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur runs the Marseille-Ventimiglia line at two to four trains an hour in daytime. From Monaco-Monte-Carlo: Cap-d'Ail 4 min, Èze-sur-Mer 9, Roquebrune-Cap-Martin 6, Menton 11, Villefranche 13, Nice-Ville 22, Ventimiglia 23, Cannes about 1h05.

other.label: The station is inside the rock
other.text: Two long exits sit several hundred metres apart: Sainte-Dévote for the port, La Condamine and the Rocher; the Ostende end for Monte-Carlo. Pick the wrong one and you climb an extra 60 m.

other.label: Tickets
other.text: TER singles come from machines or SNCF Connect: Monaco-Nice approx €5.20, Monaco-Menton approx €3. The Pass Isabelle, roughly €12-15 a day, covers unlimited TER plus Zou! and Lignes d'Azur buses across the Alpes-Maritimes and pays for itself on the Nice and Cap Ferrat days. Not valid into Italy, buy the Ventimiglia leg separately.

other.label: Buses
other.text: Compagnie des Autobus de Monaco runs six lines inside the principality: single approx €2, day pass approx €5.50, contactless accepted. Zou! line 100 shadows the coast from Nice to Menton at approx €2-3, slower than the train but scenic on the Basse Corniche.

other.label: The lifts are free
other.text: Monaco has around thirty-five public lifts and escalators linking its levels, most running 06:00 to midnight, some around the clock. They are on the free CAM map and they save enormous amounts of climbing.

other.label: Timed entry
other.text: Oceanographic Museum and the Casino daytime visit: a day or two ahead in summer. Villa Ephrussi: same week. Cap Moderne: weeks, sometimes a month.

other.label: Law and habits
other.text: Monaco enforces public decorum: no swimwear or bare chests away from the beach, and it is policed. Cards work everywhere; keep €20 in cash for market stalls and Italian bars.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 across all three countries. In Monaco, 17 for police and 18 for fire and ambulance. Sea rescue on VHF 16.

proTips: Climb the Chemin de Nietzsche from Èze-sur-Mer in the morning shade rather than descending it in the afternoon; it is loose underfoot, and the bus down from the village is easy.
The Oceanographic Museum's roof terrace and café are included in the ticket and almost nobody goes up. It is the best free-with-entry view on the Rocher.
Ventimiglia's market is Friday only and winds down by 13:00. Build the week around it if Italian produce matters.
Buy the Pass Isabelle at an SNCF machine on the Nice day and use it for the Cimiez buses too; those museums are far enough uphill to matter.
Monaco's public lift from Larvotto to Boulevard d'Italie and the one at Sainte-Dévote turn a 30-minute uphill slog into a 90-second ride. Learn those two.

packingNotes: Trail-capable shoes for the Chemin de Nietzsche and the Cap Ferrat littoral path: rock and loose stone, not promenade.
A collared shirt or equivalent for the Casino and the Métropole bar; trainers and shorts are refused after 20:00.
A passport, not just an ID card: the Casino checks it, and spot checks happen on the Ventimiglia train.
Two litres of water for the Èze and Cap Martin days; no fountains on either climb.
Sun protection in April as much as August; the reflection off the sea on these south-facing slopes is fierce.
Swimwear and a quick-dry towel; Larvotto, Plage Mala at Cap-d'Ail and Menton's Sablettes are each a short walk from a station.
whatCouldGoWrong: **You booked during Grand Prix week.** The circuit build starts about six weeks before the late-May race and stands stay up for two after. Streets close, grandstands block the harbour and rates triple. Check the ACM calendar before booking anything.
**A TER strike.** French rail strikes are common and announced days ahead. Zou! line 100 keeps running along the coast, slower but reliable.
**Cap Moderne is full.** Usually it is. Walk the free Promenade Le Corbusier instead; it passes directly below E-1027.
**Swell shuts the coastal paths.** The Sentier du Littoral at Cap-d'Ail and Cap Martin closes in heavy weather, posted at the trailheads. The Moyenne Corniche buses give the same coast from above.
**Monaco costs more than you planned.** Move two dinners to Beausoleil or Menton and one lunch to the Condamine market, and the week comes back into range.
